title: Tech Note: Using ASCII Maps to Export and Import Data on the Windows Platform
author: Jeff Browning
featured_technology: IMPORT/EXPORT TEXT, DIF, SYLK; RECEIVE/SEND PACKET

historical_commentary.text: This note documents 4D's built-in ASCII map feature for translating high-order (128-255) diacritical/symbol characters between 4D's internal Macintosh character set and the many different Windows ASCII character sets, needed whenever data was imported/exported between 4D (always Mac-encoded internally, even under Windows) and native Windows text files; this entire character-set translation problem is obsolete now that modern systems use Unicode throughout, eliminating the Mac-vs-Windows high-order ASCII mismatch altogether.
related_updates: Modern 4D and virtually all modern software use Unicode (UTF-8/UTF-16) internally and for import/export, eliminating the Macintosh-vs-Windows high-order ASCII character set mismatch this note addresses
The Altura Mac2Win porting layer that 4D for Windows historically ran on has long been retired from current 4D versions
4D's ASCII Map feature and USE ASCII MAP command reflect a pre-Unicode text encoding model no longer central to current 4D development
